name: Objection & Competitor Intelligence
tagline: Know exactly what blocks your deals
shortDescription: Tracks every objection, competitor mention, and pricing pushback across your sales calls, then aggregates them into a live intelligence feed your revenue team can act on.
longDescription:
Most sales teams learn about a new competitor talking point three weeks after it starts costing them deals — usually from an anecdote in a pipeline review. By then, dozens of calls have already gone the wrong way. Objection & Competitor Intelligence closes that gap by listening to every recorded sales call and cataloging each objection, competitor reference, and pricing concern the moment it appears in a transcript.

Homayar's analysis agents classify objections into a structured taxonomy you control: pricing, integration, security, contract terms, switching cost, and any custom categories you define. Each mention is linked back to the exact call, timestamp, and rep, so a sales leader can move from "we keep losing on price" to "price objections rose 34% this quarter, concentrated in mid-market renewals, and here are the 12 calls where reps handled it best."

The competitor layer works the same way. When a prospect names a rival, Homayar captures the context — what feature they cited, what claim they repeated, whether the rep had a response. Over weeks, this builds a verifiable map of how competitors are positioned against you in real conversations, not in analyst reports.

Nothing here is about grading individual reps. The module exists to give the whole team a shared, evidence-backed view of the market as customers actually describe it — a companion for your battlecards, not a scoreboard.
whoItsFor: Sales leaders, revenue operations managers, and product marketing teams who need objection and competitive data sourced from real calls rather than CRM notes.

Reduce time-to-updated-battlecard from weeks to days

name: Deal Risk Scoring
tagline: Hear the warning signs before forecasts slip
shortDescription: Scores every open deal for risk based on what was actually said on calls — hesitation, stalled next steps, single-threaded contacts, and unresolved objections.
longDescription:
Pipeline reviews run on what reps remember and what CRM fields say. Deals slip because of what neither captures: the prospect who stopped asking implementation questions, the champion who went quiet on the last two calls, the "we'll circle back after the board meeting" that never got a follow-up date. Deal Risk Scoring listens for these signals in the calls themselves.

For every opportunity with associated call recordings, Homayar's agents evaluate a set of conversation-derived risk factors: whether a concrete next step was agreed, whether decision-makers beyond a single contact have joined calls, whether pricing and security objections were resolved or merely deferred, and how the prospect's engagement language has shifted across the deal's call history. Each factor contributes to a 0–100 risk score with a plain-language explanation and links to the supporting call moments.

The score is built to be argued with, not obeyed. Every component is traceable to a specific exchange in a specific call, so a rep can challenge it in a pipeline review and a manager can verify it in two clicks. Teams that adopt it typically stop debating whether a deal is at risk and start debating what to do about it — which is the conversation that actually saves quarters.
whoItsFor: VPs of sales, sales managers, and revenue operations teams running weekly pipeline reviews on deals worth defending.

name: Winning Talk Patterns
tagline: Learn what your best calls do differently
shortDescription: Analyzes talk ratio, question cadence, discovery depth, and pacing across won and lost deals to identify the conversational behaviors that correlate with closing.
longDescription:
Every sales team has a top performer whose calls just work — and a coaching program built on guesses about why. Winning Talk Patterns replaces the guesses with measurement. It compares the conversational structure of calls attached to won deals against calls attached to lost ones, across your own team, in your own market.

The module measures the behaviors that research and your own data say matter: talk-to-listen ratio, how early and how often discovery questions appear, monologue length, interruption frequency, pacing of pricing discussions, and how next steps get proposed and confirmed. Rather than declaring universal rules, it surfaces the patterns that distinguish your winning calls — because the right ratio for enterprise banking software is not the right ratio for telecom renewals.

Findings flow directly into coaching. Each pattern comes with example clips from your team's strongest calls, so enablement sessions move from abstract advice ("ask better questions") to concrete demonstrations ("here are four openings where early budget questions reshaped the deal"). Reps see their own metrics privately, framed as a companion benchmark, never a leaderboard — the goal is replication of what works, not ranking of who doesn't.
whoItsFor: Sales enablement leaders, frontline sales managers, and team leads who want coaching content grounded in their own win/loss data instead of generic best practices.
keyOutcomes: Identify 5–8 statistically distinct behaviors separating won from lost calls
Shorten new-rep ramp time by up to 30% with pattern-based onboarding
Lift discovery-question rate per call by giving reps measurable targets
Build a clip library of best-practice moments from real team calls
Replace opinion-driven coaching debates with measured baselines

name: Team Pulse Dashboard
tagline: Your whole floor, one calm view
shortDescription: A live operational dashboard that rolls up call volume, sentiment, quality scores, and emerging issues across every agent and queue — built for supervisors, not surveillance.
longDescription:
Supervisors managing 15 to 50 agents make dozens of judgment calls a day with almost no real-time information: who needs help, which queue is heating up, whether this morning's product issue is spreading. Team Pulse Dashboard gives them a single screen that answers those questions as calls are analyzed, without anyone listening over anyone's shoulder.

The dashboard aggregates Homayar's per-call analysis into team-level signals: rolling sentiment by queue, quality score distribution, average handle time against baseline, first-contact resolution trends, and a live feed of detected issues ranked by frequency. When the same complaint shows up on eight calls in an hour, supervisors see it as a pattern — not as eight isolated tickets discovered tomorrow.

Individual agent views are designed around the companion principle. A supervisor sees who might benefit from support — an agent absorbing a streak of difficult calls, or one whose scores dipped after a process change — framed as a prompt to help, with the evidence attached. There are no public leaderboards, no real-time monitoring of audio, and agents can see their own data on the same terms their supervisor does. Teams adopt it faster because nobody has to be talked into being watched.
whoItsFor: Call center supervisors, team leads, and floor managers responsible for daily operational decisions across multi-agent teams.

name: Escalation Radar
tagline: Catch escalations while they're still conversations
shortDescription: Flags calls showing escalation signals — rising frustration, repeat-contact patterns, legal or churn language — so supervisors can intervene before a complaint becomes a case.
longDescription:
Most escalations are visible in the call before they become official. The customer who says "this is the third time I've called," the shift from frustration to resignation, the first mention of a regulator or a competitor — these signals are all in the audio, and they almost never make it into the wrap-up notes. Escalation Radar is the module that listens for them.

After each call is analyzed, Homayar's agents check for a configurable set of escalation indicators: sentiment trajectory across the call, repeat-contact history on the same issue, explicit cancellation or legal language, unresolved promises from prior calls, and mismatches between the customer's stated urgency and the resolution offered. Calls crossing your thresholds appear on the radar ranked by severity, each with a 30-second summary and links to the relevant moments.

The payoff is timing. A supervisor who learns about a brewing escalation the same afternoon can call the customer back, fix the process gap, or coach the handoff — quietly, before anything formal happens. Banks and insurers also use the radar's audit trail to demonstrate proactive complaint handling to regulators, with every flagged call documented from detection through resolution.
whoItsFor: Call center supervisors, escalation managers, and complaint-handling teams in regulated and high-stakes service environments.

name: Shift Handover Digests
shortDescription: Auto-generated end-of-shift summaries covering open issues, escalations in progress, notable calls, and queue health — so the next supervisor inherits context, not chaos.
longDescription:
Shift handovers in most call centers are a five-minute hallway conversation and a half-finished spreadsheet. Whatever the outgoing supervisor forgets to mention becomes the incoming supervisor's surprise: the irate customer promised a callback at 6 PM, the billing issue that generated forty calls, the new agent who struggled all afternoon and needs a check-in. Shift Handover Digests makes the handover automatic and complete.

At configurable shift boundaries, Homayar compiles everything its agents observed during the shift into a structured digest: escalations opened and their current status, recurring issues with call counts and example summaries, commitments made to customers with their deadlines, queue metrics against baseline, and notable calls worth a listen. The outgoing supervisor reviews, annotates, and sends it in two minutes instead of writing it for twenty.

For 24/7 operations — hospital lines, banking support, government services — the digest becomes the institutional memory between shifts. Nothing depends on who remembered to mention what, and a supervisor returning from two days off can read three digests and be current. Operations leaders get a searchable archive of every handover, which turns "what happened last Tuesday night?" from an investigation into a lookup.
whoItsFor: Shift supervisors and operations managers running multi-shift or 24/7 contact center operations.

Eliminate dropped customer commitments across shift boundaries
Reduce repeat-explanation calls by giving incoming staff full issue context

name: Private Deployment Package
tagline: Homayar inside your perimeter, fully managed
shortDescription: A fixed-scope implementation that deploys the complete Homayar platform into your VPC or on-premise environment, with your data never leaving your infrastructure.
longDescription:
For banks, hospitals, insurers, and government agencies, the question is rarely whether call analysis is valuable — it's whether the audio can leave the building. The Private Deployment Package answers it by not asking the data to move. Homayar's full platform — speech-to-text, the analysis agent team, scoring, dashboards, and reporting — runs inside your AWS, Azure, or GCP VPC, or on your own hardware.

The package is a defined engagement, not an open-ended consulting project. Over a typical 6–10 week timeline, our deployment engineers work with your infrastructure and security teams through four fixed phases: environment assessment and sizing, installation and telephony integration, security review support (including documentation for your internal audit), and a validated production cutover with two weeks of hypercare. You receive a runbook, architecture diagrams, and a trained internal operations contact at handoff.

Every component runs within your network boundary. Transcripts, audio, scores, and reports are stored in your databases under your encryption keys and your retention policies. Homayar's engineers access the environment only through channels you provision and audit. For organizations under GDPR, HIPAA, or national banking regulations, this is typically the difference between a stalled procurement and a signed one.

name: SSO & SCIM Provisioning
shortDescription: An identity add-on that connects Homayar to your IdP for single sign-on, automated user provisioning via SCIM, and role mapping driven by your directory groups.
longDescription:
A call analytics platform holds some of the most sensitive conversational data in your company — which makes manually managed accounts a liability your security team will rightly refuse. SSO & SCIM Provisioning brings Homayar under your existing identity governance: Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Ping, or any SAML 2.0 / OIDC-compliant provider.

Single sign-on means agents, supervisors, and analysts authenticate the way they do everywhere else, with your MFA and conditional access policies applied automatically. SCIM provisioning means lifecycle events flow without tickets: a new supervisor added to the right directory group gets the right Homayar role within minutes; a departing employee loses access the moment HR deactivates them, not three weeks later during an access review.

Role mapping is where the add-on earns its keep in large deployments. Directory groups map to Homayar roles and data scopes — a site supervisor sees their site, a QA analyst sees their assigned queues, a CX executive sees rollups without raw audio. The annual plan includes configuration support, mapping reviews at your cadence, and priority support for identity incidents, because an SSO outage on a Monday morning is not the time to open a standard ticket.

name: Dedicated Throughput Tier
tagline: Guaranteed analysis capacity at any volume
shortDescription: Reserved, contractually guaranteed processing capacity for organizations analyzing 100,000+ calls per month, with throughput SLAs, dedicated infrastructure, and a named technical account manager.
longDescription:
Shared infrastructure is the right answer until the day it isn't. A national telecom analyzing two million calls a month, a bank that needs yesterday's calls scored before the 8 AM compliance review, a retailer whose Black Friday volume triples overnight — these operations cannot queue behind anyone. The Dedicated Throughput Tier reserves processing capacity that belongs to you alone.

Your contract specifies concrete numbers: calls processed per hour, maximum time from recording ingestion to completed analysis, and burst headroom for seasonal peaks. Those numbers carry SLAs with service credits, not best-effort language. Behind them sits infrastructure provisioned for your account — isolated processing queues, dedicated transcription and agent-analysis capacity, and priority scheduling that holds your latency steady regardless of platform-wide load.

The tier includes a named technical account manager who knows your call profile, your peak calendar, and your integration topology. Quarterly capacity reviews use your actual volume trends to recommend adjustments before you hit limits — scaling is a planning conversation, not an outage retrospective. Pricing is structured per analyzed-call-hour against committed volume, and is scoped with you directly because a 100,000-call operation and a 5-million-call operation are not the same engagement.
whoItsFor: Heads of CX operations and enterprise IT at high-volume organizations — telecoms, national banks, large insurers, and government service lines — where analysis latency is an operational dependency.
